challenges.name: detect-breaking-changes-review
challenges.title: Detect breaking changes: is this diff safe?
challenges.description: A pull request only adds things to a response schema, and the reviewer approves it as safe. Two statements on the diff and the Android model that reads the response.

questions.explanation: False. For a client that reads the response, a new enum value is a value it has never seen. Android 3.9 decodes level into a closed Kotlin enum with three entries, so the first course with level "expert" fails to decode, just like a missing field. Adding an enum value is safe in a request (the server learns to accept more) and breaking in a response read by exhaustive clients, unless every client was built with an unknown-value fallback. The misconception is to judge a change by "added or removed" instead of by who reads it and what they can handle.

True. The old schema promised a number in every response, and 3.9 declares averageRating as a non-nullable Double. The first course without reviews sends null and decoding fails. For response readers, a schema that accepts more values is a promise of fewer guarantees: became-nullable is breaking, while the opposite (removing null) is safe. In OpenAPI 3.1 nullability is part of the type list, so a diff that looks like a pure addition can be the breaking change. The new optional badges property, on the other hand, is safe for 3.9, which ignores unknown keys.

challenges.name: detect-breaking-response-changes
challenges.title: Detect breaking changes in a response schema
challenges.description:
After the course DTO incident, CodeDev wants CI to compare the response schema of every endpoint on main with the one in a pull request and fail on changes that break clients that READ responses (the web app, the Android apps, partner integrations). Write compareSchemas(oldSchema, newSchema).

Schema subset (OpenAPI 3.1 = JSON Schema): every node has "type", a string or a non-empty array of "string", "number", "integer", "boolean", "object", "array", "null" (nullable = "null" in the list). A node may have "properties", "required", "enum" and "items". Inputs guarantee: no $ref; an array node has "items" on both sides; an enum is on both sides of a compared pair or on neither.

Walk both schemas from the root (path "") and compare the old and the new node at each path:
1. "null" added to the type -> breaking "became-nullable"; removed -> safe "no-longer-nullable".
2. The other types (without "null", sorted, joined by ",") differ -> breaking "type-changed" with detail "<old> -> <new>", e.g. "integer -> string" or "integer -> integer,number". Every difference counts, even a widening. Nothing below this node is compared.
3. Enum: each value only in the new enum -> breaking "enum-value-added" (CodeDev's Android apps decode enums into closed Kotlin enum classes, so an unknown value fails); each value only in the old enum -> safe "enum-value-removed". The detail is the JSON text of the value: "\"expert\"" for a string, "4" for a number.
4. Object (when the types include "object"): for each old property missing in the new schema -> breaking "property-removed" (required or not: a client may read it), and nothing below it; for each property in both: required in old but not in new -> breaking "became-optional", the opposite -> safe "became-required", then compare the two property schemas at <path>/properties/<name>; each property only in the new schema -> safe "property-added" (required or not).
5. Array (when the types include "array"): compare the items at <path>/items.

Paths are JSON Pointers into the schema document; in a property name "~" becomes "~0" and "/" becomes "~1" ("title/vi" -> "/properties/title~1vi").

Output: { "breaking": Change[], "safe": Change[] } with Change = { "path", "change", "detail"? } ("detail" only for type-changed, enum-value-added and enum-value-removed). Sort each list by path, then change, then detail, comparing strings by UTF-16 code units (the < and > operators, not localeCompare).

Invalid input: throw an Error when a node the comparison reaches has no "type", an empty type array or an unknown type name; the test runner then prints { "error": "invalid schema" }.

Input (stdin, JSON): { "old": Schema, "new": Schema }.
hints: For each kind of change, ask: can a client that was correct yesterday fail on today's response? A response that may contain more values (null, a new enum value, another type) or fewer fields is the dangerous direction.

Write one recursive function that takes the old node, the new node and the current path. Handle null first, then the other types (and return early when they differ), then enum, then properties and required, then items. Collect into two arrays and sort once at the end.

A similar case on other input: old { type: "object", properties: { a: { type: "integer" } }, required: ["a"] }, new { type: ["object", "null"], properties: { a: { type: "string" }, b: { type: "string" } } } gives breaking: "" became-nullable, "/properties/a" became-optional, "/properties/a" type-changed "integer -> string"; safe: "/properties/b" property-added.

Leaderboard list: changes inside array items, required lists and a cursor
